Name: Matthew Manning
Question: Why can't we just let Hillary Clinton run again in 2020? Wouldn’t so many people love to see her beat Trump?
Answer: That would be the worst political slaughter of this generation. Back in 2016, Hillary had absolutely every possible advantage over Trump: Honestly, I don’t blame the Huffington Post for getting this wrong. Hillary clearly had every advantage over Donald going into the election. But she still lost. And not by just a handful of electoral votes; Trump decimated Hillary, picking up a full 74 votes more than her. Now, let’s take a look at the 2020 election. Like him or not, Trump has had a pretty spectacular first 2 years in office. The economy is doing better than it ever has in the last decade, investors are excited, unemployment is down, Trump has successfully gotten two Justices on the Supreme Court, and the North Korea situation has been handled. Trump even managed to not only retain but gain seats in the senate during the midterms, and much of the House was lost to the Democrats simply because Republicans were retiring. Obama didn’t manage to have midterms anywhere near as fruitful as Trump. So now Trump has a strong political track record. Not without scandal, but certainly strong in the eyes of anyone who voted for him. And on top of that, in 2020 Trump will be running as the incumbent. And incumbents always have an advantage over the new guy. We saw what Trump did to Hillary when she had every advantage over him. Imagine what he would’ve done if he had every advantage over her. The only way this could possibly work for Hillary is if Trump monumentally crashes and burns over the next two years. Then Hillary might be able to ride back in on her high-horse saying “I told you so!” and the voters just might believe her. But as it looks now, Trump isn’t going to crash and burn. And Hillary could never even dream of beating him.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: Why are Americans so obsessed with guns and the 2nd amendment? And before anyone rants on about rights and freedom, what about the right to life and the freedom to live in peace and safety?
Answer: The media has blown gun-related violence way out of proportion. They’ve made people think it’s something like a car accident; common, completely random, could happen to you or any of your loved ones at any time. This just isn’t the case. For starters, nearly 2/3rds of all American gun deaths are suicides. You could make the argument that we should ban guns to decrease the suicide rate, but that’s a separate argument from saying we should ban guns for people’s right to be safe. And out of the 37% of gun deaths that are homicides, the vast majority are gang related. Have you ever listened to rap music? It’s hard to find a rapper who doesn’t talk about guns. They’re not just talking; gang related gun violence is a massive driving force in US gun statistics. That might sound scary to you, but keep in mind that almost all gang-related violence is gang member on gang member. It’s very rare for civilians to be injured in these conflicts. So by simply not joining a gang, you bring your chances of being a victim of gang violence down to basically zero (shocking right). And now for the mother of all gun issues: mass shootings. This is the one which actually is like a car accident. The victims are random and they don’t know it’s coming. However, mass shootings are EXTREMELY rare. Depending on the definition you use anywhere between 85 and 373 people died from mass shootings in 2018. And no I’m not missing a zero on either of those numbers. To put that in perspective, roughly 61,000 people in the US died of the flu during the 2017-2018 season. But most of us don’t worry about the flu at all. Many of us don’t even get flu shots. Even by the highest measure of mass shooting deaths, you still have a literally 1-in-a-million chance of being killed in a mass shooting. That’s not something worth losing sleep over. You have a significantly greater chance of dying from the flu, getting in a car crash, drinking yourself to death, drowning, and even choking to death on your food. If none of those things keep you up at night, gun violence shouldn’t either.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: Why is there stigma in the black community of being a Republican?
Answer: Being black in America comes with a handful of statistical disadvantages. You’re more likely to experience police brutality. You’re more likely to get harsher sentences than white people for the same crime, even if it’s your first offense. And if you have a particularly black-sounding name, you’re less likely to get a call back on your resume than if your name sounded white. But while these are all unjust events, they aren’t what stops most black people from succeeding in America. They’re examples of the stigma against blacks. But why does that stigma exist? The answer is money. The median black household net worth is only $1700 as of 2013. The median white household net worth at the same time was $116,800. That’s the true racial gap in America. Racism does exist, but it’s no longer the real obstacle in the black community’s path. The vast majority of black people’s lives will not be negatively impacted by police brutality and longer prison sentences. And make no mistake, these are unjust problems that we need to work to solve - but when it comes to median black success, they aren’t the primary obstacle. A lack of family wealth to fall back on or build from is. The despair of feeling you have nothing and no opportunity is what leads to crime, which leads to stigma against the entire community. The correct approach to solving this inequality if for the black community to recognize the opportunity we have now. The median black household net worth is the result of historical discrimination, but that discrimination is largely no more. Experiencing racism as a black person is usually more of an annoyance than something life-threatening. We are in a position to secure wealth for our families and elevate our community. We have the power to rectify history. And this is a classic republican message: pull yourself up by your bootstraps. The reason this message is so stigmatized in the black community is because it often comes across as dismissive. A lot of the time it’s said by white people in response to black people attempting to address problems of police brutality/modern racism. There’s this air of “stop complaining and go work.” What Republicans need to realize is the pull yourself up by your bootstraps message is compatible with fighting for better criminal justice and less discrimination. In order to have a true meritocracy, we have to eliminate as much unjust discrimination as possible. An injustice anywhere is an injustice everywhere. And what’s funny is that Republicans already agree with most of what groups like BLM are fighting for: most Republicans dislike police/state overreach and fear tyranny, believe in the rule of law, and want equal standards for everyone. But both sides have gotten defensive and closed off to each other. In order for the message of individualism and opportunity to be effectively delivered to the communities who need it the most, it has to be delivered with empathy. Many black people feel being right-wing means dismissing the historical struggle of our people. This is why black right-wingers are so frequently attacked for our views; they’re taken as an attack to the entire black community and our ancestors. As right-wingers we need to do a better job at saying “Yes, there is discrimination we need to eliminate. It is unjust. But what will ultimately lead to black success in America is for the entire community to work to secure wealth for themselves and grow their assets.” There isn’t much the state can do for the black community - pulling ourselves out of this position ultimately falls on our own shoulders. And when we realize that, and recognize just how capable we are of achieving all of this, that’s when things will start to change. And as conservatives, we understand this. But many black people have never been properly exposed to these ideas. It is our job to propagate this ideology. And not just for the benefit of the black community - less inner city crime is good for everyone. More home ownership and entrepreneurship is good for everyone. More people striving for the American Dream is better for all of America. The American Dream isn’t dead, but many people have lost faith in it. And right-wingers are in a position to restore that faith through our ideology. So let’s go out there and improve the world.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: What is something you wish people would stop saying?
Answer: Today, I wish people (especially teenagers) would stop saying “Go vote!” I wrote an answer a while back about how nothing you say on the internet about politics matters until you put it into practice and vote. And that’s true. But there’s voting, and then there’s whipping yourself up into a frenzy over people voting or not voting. This is a story I screenshotted from some girl I happen to follow. I went ahead and scribbled/added the emoji to protect her privacy. It was one of three pictures of her pointing a gun at a camera and telling people to vote. And after the third picture? I laughed a little to myself about this girl feeling the need to insert her gun control opinion into her voting plea, but mostly I just felt annoyed. These thousands (or millions) of young people around the country aren’t saying “go vote” because they want young people to express their views. They’re saying “go vote” because they think young people will vote the same way they do. And that’s fine, morally. It’s just annoying. No one needs a hundred reminders on the day of the elections to go vote - the people who were gonna vote had already decided they would, and the people who weren’t aren’t gonna be persuaded by an angry last-minute plea for them to get to the polls (“or die”). What you’re really doing is virtue signaling. “I’m woke! I’m a member of The Resistance! I don’t just vote, I mobilize other people to vote!” Yeah, you’re a real civil rights activist for putting “Go vote!” on your Instagram story. At the end of the day, it’s just another election. The sun will rise tomorrow, the birds will chirp, people will go to work, and the world will keep on spinning, like it has for the last 4 1/2 billion years. Feel free to vote, but calm the hell down.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: It seems the Republicans have a line that is ‘too far’ (white supremacy, Neo Nazis, most on the right and left agree that’s too far and unacceptable.) where is the Lefts line? What is viewed as extreme and unacceptable to them on their side?
Answer: It’s laughable how many Leftists are answering this question defensively, going so far as to deny any extremism on the Left entirely. And it only proves how important this question actually is. Both sides of the political aisle are fully capable of taking their ideologies to the extreme. And it’s important to recognize when an ideology becomes extreme because, if left unchecked, extremist ideologies kill people. Here’s a bunch of pictures of the Gulags to prove my point: Now, I think any reasonable person can agree that what you’re seeing in these images is wrong. And not wrong in an “Oh, they made some mistakes but we’ll have another election soon and vote them out” kind of wrong. It’s wrong in the undeniably inhumane and purely evil sense of the word. And that was a result of extremism on the Left. A lot of the Leftists answering this question have adamantly stated “Well we don’t have any communists running for democratic offices!” First of all, congratulations! Really, tremendous job on not having anyone openly run with the goal to institute an ideology that killed easily 100 million people in the 20th century. But the thing is, no one instrumental in the rise of communism was planning to kill 100 million people. That wasn’t communism’s goal. And that’s exactly the problem with defining Left Wing extremism. With Right Wing extremism, it’s pretty clean cut: people could tell right off the bat that Hitler’s intentions were bad. Churchill warned us about him back in the 30s. Many of the Jews in Germany were lucky enough to move out before the rounding ups and mass executions started; they could sense the evil intentions in the air, long before any evil actions had taken place. Left wing extremism is more complex. Right wing extremism has an open hatred of “the other” and promises a utopia for the preferred group if they lash out at this other. Left wing extremism has the same hatred and makes the same promises, but this hatred is concealed. It’s hidden behind a rationalization of perceived injustices. Marxism. It’s an ideology founded on the hatred of the rich, the bourgeoisie. The idea being that, because all men are created equal, those who end up above others must have committed some sort of injustice to get there. “Let the proletariat rise up and overthrow the bourgeoisie, and there shall be equality and prosperity for all.” This is what Lenin promised. And the images above are what Lenin’s words ultimately delivered. Some of the first people to be killed off by communism were the most successful Ukrainian farmers. These people were not anywhere near rich by today’s standards; they simply had a bit of land, maybe a cow, and more than enough crops to both sell and feed their families. Yet all of their crops were stolen from them and taken to the “redistribution centers” to be redistributed. After all, the people must collectively own the means of production, right? The result was 12 million farmers starving to death. This famine is known as the Holodomor and is recognized as a genocide upon the Ukrainian people committed by the Soviet Union. What makes Leftist extremism so dangerous is that it effectively masquerades as love for the downtrodden when it is actually hatred for the successful. The intellectual socialists do not especially love the poor, they simply despise the rich. Ideologies founded in hatred easily become murderous. Communism has been thoroughly bashed throughout the 20th century. Those who speak in terms of “the bourgeoisie” and “the proletariat” are no longer taken as seriously as they once might’ve been. But the ideology hasn’t died; it has simply switched its terms. “The bourgeoisie” is now “the 1%.” And Marxism has expanded past its original economic ideology and into issues of race, gender, and sexuality, merging with post-modernism to become Cultural Marxism. If you’ve been on Twitter in the last 5 years, I’m sure you’ve seen it: “I hate white people” “I hate men” “I hate straight people” “I hate cis people.” These are some of the new terms for the bourgeoisie; for the privilieged classes that are presumed to oppress “the other.” Cultural Marxism and Nazism are two sides of the same coin; where Nazis speak for the preferred group and tell them to lash out at the other, (Cultural) Marxists claim to speak for the other and tell them to lash out at the preferred group. They’re both hate-founded ideologies, on opposite sides of the political spectrum. And I’m sure there will be Leftists who read this and feel the need to reiterate “But there are no democratic officials who are communists!! The extremism is there on the right, but it isn’t there on the left!” This is Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. If you follow politics at all, you’ve probably heard of her. She’s a young up-and-comer in the DNC. She’s also a Cultural Marxist and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America. And if you paid any attention in your high school history class, you’ll recognize this man. Vladimir Lenin, laying out the point more concisely than I ever could. Now, before you start smashing the keyboard explaining to me that Alexandria O-C is a “Democratic” Socialist, ask yourself what you would think of me if I told you I was a “Democratic” Nazi. And keep in mind that O-C has heaped lavish praise upon the likes of Venezuela, an actual socialist country with citizens who are currently starving. There is extremism on the right. There is extremism on the Left. They’re two sides of the same coin, both founded on hatred. And for the good of our country, our people, and the world at large, we need to learn to recognize hatred on both sides of the aisle.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: Does it bother you that America is the laughing stock of the developed world currently?
Answer: Imagine the world as a high school, and the countries as students. America is the hot rich popular jock who everyone loves to hate. He pulls up to school everyday in his Porsche and double parks it. He dates the hottest girl in school and has the other girls fawning over him. He’s a star athlete. He gets away with everything. He’s a jerk. And people never fail to point that out. They say “he isn’t even that smart. He doesn’t deserve what he has. He’s a douche. He’s an asshole. I fucking hate that guy.” But at the end of the day, they’re still clamoring for his approval. They copy all the trends he starts. They all want to be invited to his lavish parties. They all cheer for him when he scores the winning touchdown. The guys want to be him and the girls want to be with him. Maybe he is a jerk. Maybe he really isn’t that smart. Maybe he really doesn’t deserve what he has. But at the end of the day, he still has it. He’s still that guy. He still has his Porsche. His girls. His parties. His stardom. Could he do better? Be better? Absolutely. But he’s not really hated for his flaws. Everyone has flaws. He’s hated for the success he has inspite of his flaws. So, does it bother me that America is the laughing stock of the world? Not in the slightest.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: What's your opinion on Kavanaugh's confirmation?
Answer: I have mixed feelings on Kavanaugh’s confirmation. For starters, whether you believe Ford’s testimony or not, there was nowhere near enough evidence to convict Kavanaugh. Further FBI investigations would be unlikely to uncover any further evidence against him; the events in question happened over three decades ago and had no eye-witnesses. I would be highly opposed to having a convicted rapist on the Supreme Court. But alleged is not the same as convicted. Trump was right when he said “Guilty until proven innocent is a very dangerous precedent for this country.” Sure, if you’re a leftist you might’ve enjoyed it now, had it been used to convict Kavanaugh. But would you have liked it if the tables were turned? What if you were accused of a crime, sexual or otherwise, and you had to prove your innocence rather than the prosecution having to prove your guilt? Leftists frequently talk about black men being put in unfair trial situations and convicted too often/sentenced too harshly. A “guilty until proven innocent” precedent would only exacerbate this problem. Then there’s the matter of the Democrats’ behavior throughout this whole process. It was a hideously thinly-veiled power play. I don’t think a single Democrat actually gave a damn about whether or not Kavanaugh was guilty. They saw an opportunity to keep a justice they didn’t like off the Court, and they took it. It’s no coincidence that the Democrats waited until right before the midterm elections before bringing these allegations to light. At best, they would’ve delayed Kavanaugh’s confirmation, hopefully regained a Senate majority, and prevented him from ever being confirmed. At worst, they would rile up their base and hopefully improve their midterm numbers. This wasn’t about justice or ideology for them; it was pure politics. And with Republicans now increasingly riled up about midterms, and Kavanaugh confirmed, their plan seems to have backfired completely. And I’m glad for that; the Dems certainly deserve a political lashing for their behavior. But then there’s the matter of how Kavanaugh was confirmed. It wasn’t by a 60 vote majority, which is the traditional number for confirming a justice. The Republicans utilized the “nuclear option” to allow for a simple 51-vote majority to confirm Kavanaugh. This “nuclear option” was a precedent set by the Obama administration when they were frustrated with the Republican’s efforts to delay their justice’s confirmations. The 60 vote majority rule was put in place to deter the appointment of ideologically biased candidates. While I don’t necessarily think Kavanaugh falls into this category, this is a dangerous precedent to set. The amount of power concentrated at the federal government has been increasing from the start of the 20th century. While it might currently be affecting mostly State’s rights, if we continue down this path there will come a time when this concentration of power begins to strip us, as citizens, of our own personal liberties. And making it easier for either party to appoint ideologically biased justices will only increase this power at the federal level. So despite the fact that, as a conservative, I’m happy about Kavanaugh’s confirmation for a large number of reasons, I’m absolutely not happy with this “nuclear option” precedent. When (and I do say when, because the day will come sooner or later) the Democrats are in power again, they will absolutely use this precedent against the Republicans. And I’m not looking forward to that day. EDIT: As has been pointed out in the comments, Kavanaugh’s hearing was not a criminal prosecution. However, the burden of proof should still fall on the accuser. Our legal system works that way because it is more fair than the alternative; it’s much harder to prove innocence than it is to prove guilt. Pointing out that “there’s no innocent until proven guilty for a job hearing” doesn’t mean there shouldn’t be.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: What would you say to the young people of the USA to get them to vote?
Answer: Your opinion doesn’t matter. You can bitch and moan all day on Twitter if you want to. Maybe you’ll get a few retweet’s and followers. Maybe it’ll even make you famous. But it won’t matter. As the 2016 election was approaching, Twitter and the internet at large was chock full of people having debate upon debate about Trump, Hillary, and which of the two should/would/and even could be elected. None of it mattered. You can have your opinion. You can broadcast it to millions. You can band together in protest and shout it in the streets. You can literally shout it from the rooftops. But none of it will matter. Because at the end of the day, your opinion doesn’t matter until you put it into practice and vote. Words don’t actually change history; actions do. Words might inspire change, but what actually changes history is actions. So before the upcoming election, remember that your opinion doesn’t matter. You can be a liberal, a conservative, a libertarian, a neo-nazi, a radical-Islamist, or anything else. It’s all just words. When the next election comes, put your words into action. Vote.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: Is generation Z more conservative than previous generations? Why or why not?
Answer: As a whole, Gen Z is significantly more conservative than our millennial counterparts. But I’ve noticed that our political positions are split largely on one key demographic: Gender. Almost every single straight male friend I have (around my age) is conservative. Regardless of race. I’ve even encountered/am friends with a couple gay males who have started to lean conservative. I’ve noticed that straight men tend to have different “triggers” that shift their political views from left to right depending on their race. All of them involve feminism & identity politics. For straight white men, the motivation is obvious; why would you subscribe to a political doctrine in which you’re the villain for factors entirely out of your control? They tend to start experiencing the negative side of feminism/identity politics in high school or college, and this pushes them away from the left and inspires them to look into conservative policies. For straight black men, it’s a little more complicated. A lot of us experience the same things straight white men experience politically, and get pushed to the right in the same way. For others, police brutality tends to be the key issue; many black men are anti-republican because they don’t like the republican stance on police brutality. Other black men become conservative because they think “why are feminists busy complaining about trans bathrooms when people like me are literally being KILLED by the police?” This is another way they’re turned off by the left. For straight Asian men, it’s probably simplest of all: affirmative action. These men tend to fit the Asian stereotype of a perfect GPA and multiple extracurriculars, and then find out that they’re at a significant disadvantage when applying for college based solely on their skin color. When they realize feminism is behind this, they gravitate away from the left. But there’s also an overarching appeal of conservatism to young men that a lot of people overlook: purpose. A lot of boys, myself included, have felt sort of “lost” in the world. The girls are being encouraged to become doctors and scientists and lawyers, even though for as long as we can remember the girls have always had better grades than the boys in our classes. It feels like we’ve been left behind to figure out life for ourselves. Like there’s no role for men to fulfill anymore, and maybe we should just give up trying and resort to escapism. Conservatism provides an answer to that problem. Jordan Peterson is the personification of this, and it’s why his appeal is so huge among males my age. Conservativism gives us purpose. It tells us that we’re capable of pulling ourselves up by our bootstraps, adopting responsibility, slaying dragons, and becoming a beacon of strength for our friends, family, and society to depend on. There are far more reasons for Gen Zs being conservative that I won’t touch on in depth; after seeing our brothers, sisters, cousins, aunts, and uncles trust the system and end up unemployed and in debt, we’re definitely a lot less trusting of the state and have libertarian leanings regardless of gender. But the main conservative demographic of our generation is the young straight men who are pushed away from the left and looking for our purpose. Conservatism helps us find it.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: What is your opinion on the "Believe Women" movement?
Answer: Let’s talk about the Kavanaugh allegations. I’m not here to argue that he’s innocent. Nor am I here to argue he’s guilty. I’ll leave that to the courts. I’m here because, to the vast majority of the liberals with an opinion on this case, Kavanaugh’s guilt or innocence doesn’t matter. This case is just one in a series of battles. Battles in an ideological war. Take a look at this story I saw on Instagram: Obviously she’s talking about the Kavanaugh case. But notice what she’s focusing on. It’s not the evidence against him. It’s not analysis of the witness’ statements. It’s not even a smearing of Kavanaugh’s overall character. Notice one sentence in particular: “American society does not care about women.” To the millions of men and women (but mostly women) who are ready to believe the allegations against Kavanaugh without any substantial evidence, this case isn’t about him. This case isn’t even about his victim. It’s about how American society systematically oppresses women. Convicting Kavanaugh means getting justice for all of those women who haven’t gotten it. And I can understand how this is an appealing message for women. I’ve had 4 female friends tell me about times when they were sexually assaulted or raped. All of them are in high school. None of their rapists were reported or punished. Sexual assault is a serious problem, and we do need to do better as a society at dealing with it. But we need to do it the right way. We need to do it with evidence. We need to do it with a proper trial. We need to do it without making every case a battle in an ideological war. Because if we keep going down this path, where we believe the allegations of the accuser simply because they are the accuser, we won’t be getting justice. We’ll be getting revenge. And those aren’t the same thing.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: Would you care if Trump was assassinated? The majority of sensible people would prefer him gone.
Answer: Yes, because that is not the basis on which we decide to murder someone. I’m not a frothing-at-the-mouth Trump fan, although I do like a lot of his politics. But let’s set aside political leanings here. And let’s set aside the fact that the country would be thrown into chaos for weeks (likely months) if this were to actually happen (which means everyone would end up caring, sensible or not). Let’s take a look at why you should care if Trump is assassinated, regardless of your political leanings or opinions of him. You could’ve phrased your question as “Would you care if Trump was assassinated?” But you added a second part to it. A part that heavily implies that, since “the majority of sensible people” want him gone, his assassination wouldn’t really matter. “Sensible people” is a subjective term. Who gets to define what it means to be a sensible person? Ok, maybe you’d argue that the majority of a population gets to define it. Fair enough. You’ve just identified the greatest danger of democracy: Mob rule. Let’s say 90% of the country decided tomorrow that they wanted you dead. Would they have the right to kill you? And if you said no, would it change your mind if I told you that “the majority of sensible people” are part of that 90%? Trump is, fundamentally, a human being. Just like you. Just like me. Just like every other human being who has ever existed or ever will exist. In our legal system, violent force against another is only justified in self-defence or in the defence of other’s lives. Trump is not a murderer. Despite what Buzzfeed might have you believe, Trump is not “literally Hitler.” If a person were to assassinate Trump, they should face the full prosecution of the law. They are subject to the same standard we are all subject to. Now you might be thinking, “Yeah yeah, it’s illegal and rule of law matters and all that. But why should I care if Trump is assassinated?” You should care because you’re a citizen of this country. You, just like me, are responsible for supporting the rule of law in this country. Why? Because it benefits us. Having laws that protect us against murder is a good thing that we should all strive to enforce. And if that STILL isn’t enough for you, Trump is a human being. I get that you don’t know him personally, and I get that you don’t like him. But he’s still a human being. He has a family. He has hopes and dreams. And most importantly, he has an intrinsic right to life. You should care about that right to life being violated. We all should. Because it doesn’t take much for society to become rampantly murderous if we don’t.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: What is your opinion on abortion?
Answer: I’m going to say something that nobody likes saying or hearing: The real reason the left wants abortion to be legal is because abortion absolves women from the primary consequence of sex: pregnancy. Forget the medically extreme cases here. Yes, a small percentage of abortions are done because the mother’s life is severely in danger. Yes, an even smaller percentage of abortions are done because the fetus is already dead. The vast majority of abortions are done out of what boils down to convenience. I’m 17. I’ve already experienced this attitude toward abortion multiple times from female friends who’ve had pregnancy scares. “If I’m pregnant, I’m getting an abortion.” They’ve said. With no hesitation. It was as casual for them as deciding to get their appendix out. Probably even more so. Don’t believe me? Take a look at this meme I found scrolling through Instagram the other day: Sure, call it anecdotal evidence. Even though the tweet has 15.4k likes, and the picture has 7,262 likes. And no, the person tweeting doesn’t run that meme account, so it’s unlikely those likes overlap. But it is anecdotal, and I can’t dispute that. Instead, I can show you the cold, hard, statistics: roughly 74% of abortions are done out of convenience to the mother. Sure, those statistics are from 2004. But the attitude toward abortions has only become more casual over the last 14 years. And those statistics are from self-reporting would-be mothers. I’d imagine women having abortions for convenience reasons are less eager to report that than those who aren’t. I want to clarify that I’m not dismissing the predicament these women are in by calling their decision to get an abortion “convenience based.” A lot of these reasons are financially or emotionally driven, and I do empathize with the women who are in these situations. Having a child will uproot your life in ways very few things can. But the fact that your life will be negatively impacted by your child does not give you the right to kill it. Not having sex before marriage originated for exactly this reason: to protect against the negative consequences of sex, primarily pregnancy. The left is in a position where they want to tell women that sex can be fun and consequence-free, when that simply has never been the reality. Legal abortion is a way to mediate the consequences and further “liberate” women. At this point, the problem isn’t just in banning or legalizing abortion. Completely depriving women of abortions at this point would only mean hundreds of thousands of more unwanted children born each year. The problem lies in the societal attitude toward abortion, and toward child-rearing and adopting responsibility in general. There would need to be a massive cultural shift in order to reduce the 600,000+ abortions that are currently being had every year. The vast majority of which are, again, being done for convenience sake. My opinion on abortion is that is it a symptom and enabler of a massively flawed societal viewpoint. A deep-rooted social attitude that has driven and continues to drive the destruction of the family unit. One that I’m not certain of how to solve. But what I am certain of is that the overwhelming majority of abortions are murder. And not murders of passion; murders driven simply by convenience. If that doesn’t send a bit of a chill down your spine, I don’t know what will.

Name: Matthew Manning
Question: Why is it so difficult to implement honest democracy?
Answer: It isn’t. The problem is making sure that “honest democracy” doesn’t tear society to shreds. People misunderstand democracy. It sounds great in theory: the citizens of a country having full control of their country through their votes. The problem is that “the citizens” don’t have control; the majority does. That’s mob rule. The danger of democracy is that the majority will vote in their own best interest, and those interests may not be in line with the minority. The communist revolution was an exercise in mob rule. The first thing they did was punish and kill the successful (minority) in the interest of the non-successful class (majority). Question: How real is the belief that many colleges are fiercely liberal and are extremely unwelcoming to conservative thought?

And let’s not be blind here; this isn’t necessarily an inherent trait of liberals and progressives. Some liberals are not hostile to those with different viewpoints. And some conservatives are. But people naturally gravitate toward those with similar opinions and world views. So when you’re in an environment where the overwhelming majority of both your teachers and classmates disagree with your views, and when you’re in a political climate as polarized as ours, you’re going to suffer. Partially due to outright hostility from your classmates (and some more extreme teachers), but more importantly because of favoritism that your views will disqualify you from the minute you vocalize them.

Question: Can we please stop pretending that institutionalized racism doesn’t exist?

Question: What do conservatives find wrong with liberals?

Question: What do conservatives think of this article: I Don't Know How To Explain To You That You Should Care About Other People?
Answer: I think the author makes the same mistake a lot of liberals make when it comes to money: “If everyone who can afford to just gives a tiny bit more, all of our problems will be solved!” If economics were really that simple, we would’ve done this a long time ago. But everything is a tradeoff. The author starts out by claiming that McDonald’s workers could comfortably feed their families if we all just put up with a 4.3% price increase per item (“17 more cents for your Big Mac!! That’s nothing!!”). They link to a study to back that up. What the author fails to mention is that the 4.3% price hike is estimated by a study on what would happen if we raised the minimum wage to $15/hour (doubling it). Which means that while the difference in price is only 17 cents per Big Mac for us, the difference in price for McDonald’s is $7.25 per hour per worker. Assuming the average McDonald’s employee works 30 hours a week, 50 weeks a year, the actual difference in cost to McDonald’s is $10,875 per year per employee. Not just a measly 17 cents anymore, right? This is where I’m the sure author would chime in and say “But McDonald’s can afford it! They make billions of dollars every year!” First of all, even though McDonald’s makes over 6 billion a year it only keeps a bit over 1 billion of that in profits. The rest goes to advertising, research and development, paying their employees, etc. Still think they can just magically piss out an extra 10k per worker? But let’s assume they can. Because if the minimum wage were raised, they would probably find a way to afford it and survive. What happens to all the businesses who can’t afford it? Should they just go out of business for not being bigger? How does that help their employees feed their families? Or should they be allowed to pay their employees less than what liberals call “a living wage” just because they’re smaller? How is that ethical? And how is that fair to the bigger companies who are now forced to roll out millions more a year and are competing with people who get to pay their workers 50% less? Furthermore, every company needs to accumulate excess revenue in order to grow. Research and developing, advertising, opening new locations, all of these things cost money. By eating away at companies’ profits, you’re stripping them of their ability to grow. And if a company isn’t growing, it’s shrinking. I would be perfectly comfortable paying an extra 17 cents for my Big Mac if that were actually all it would take for McDonald’s workers to get out of poverty. But that’s not all it would take. The actual measures would be far more drastic and potentially detrimental to the economy long term. That’s when I stop being comfortable. Here’s the lesson liberals need to learn: just because you’re acting out of compassion doesn’t mean you’re doing the right thing.

Question: Do American conservatives believe that minorities are crying wolf when it comes to racism or is it more a feeling of life's not fair, get over it?

Black people aren’t doing great (collectively) in America because many of us have been living in poverty or near poverty for multiple generations. White people in similar situations aren’t doing much better, but they’re a much smaller segment of the white population so it’s less noticeable. For any black person (or other minority) who feels oppressed due to their race, know this: if you set goals for yourself and work hard for them, you will accomplish them. Racism is a mental block more than anything else. Don’t waste your life demanding better treatment from the people in power; they have no incentive to give it to you, and no real way to do so anyway. Become powerful and take what you deserve.

Question: What is your opinion of SJWs accusing people of "cultural appropriation" as if it is an inherently malicious act?
Answer: Depending on the SJW, it’s either a passive-aggressive display of their deep-rooted resentment of white people, or well-intentioned nonsense. Modern day feminism has a very heavy Marxist influence. Marxism posits two classes of people: the bourgeoisie and the proletariat, or rather the oppressor and the oppressed. The idea is that the oppressers gained everything on the backs of the oppressed. A wealthy business owner is only wealthy because he had other people work to produce things for him, and so on. In the SJW ideology, the same oppressor/oppressed belief exists. But they’ve broadened it far past class to include race, gender, sexuality, religion, and probably more that I’m unaware of. The same way Marxism assumes those in power are only in power because they’ve oppressed the people who aren’t, SJWs assume white, straight, preferably Protestant (or at least Christian) men are in power only because they’ve oppressed the people who aren’t those things (like women, racial minorities, etc). So when a non-SJW sees a white girl wearing a sombrero at her sorority’s cinco de mayo party, they see an ordinary young woman having a good time with her friends. When an SJW sees her, they see a white oppressor participating in a culture that they not only have no connection to, but have directly benefited from oppressing. This is what leads to the resentment. “Why should they get to take part in a culture if they oppressed and continue to benefit from oppressing the people in that culture!???!!” And thus, the notion of cultural appropriation is born. You’ll notice non-oppressor classes of people are almost never ever ever called out for cultural appropriation. That’s because SJWs don’t resent them; they bond over perceived shared oppression. The issue with this argument is of course that white people aren’t in power only because of oppressing people. That’s a very very small part of it. SJWs love to say “America was built on the back of slavery”, but that really isn’t true. Was it a big part of our economy for a while? Yes. Would America still exist, with similar assets and white people still in power, if we had never kept slaves? Also yes. At a certain point we have to stop blaming people for their success. White people are in power because they were able to colonize non-whites. They were able to do that because they had better technology and military. How are either of those things bad? Better yet, aren’t both of things worthy of praise? Furthermore, can you really say non-whites wouldn’t have been the colonizers if they had developed the technology first? That’s just how life goes. The biggest kid on the playground pushes the smaller kids around. That doesn’t mean it’s bad that he’s bigger, it just means he needs to stop pushing the smaller kids around. And that’s what white people did when they ended colonialism over half a century ago. As for the more mild-mannered SJWs, they view cultural appropriation as a mockery or trivialization of that culture. For them it’s just another disrespectful but well-intentioned thing that “those silly whites” do, like complimenting a black person on being well-spoken. The issue here is defining trivializing. How does a non-Mexican wearing a sombrero trivialize that culture? A common example here is the term “spirit animal”. Native Americans have to go through years of searching and various tests to discover their spirit animal. Cultural appropriators just have to pick an animal they like. I would argue that this does nothing to take away from the significance of the Native American’s spirit animal. It’s just a different approach to a similar concept. Kind of like how gay marriage doesn’t take away from straight marriage; just because people are breaking rules you follow and they don’t, doesn’t mean they’re taking away from your rules. You’re still just as free to follow them as they are theirs. Cultural appropriation is nonsense to me no matter how I look at it. And according to the SJWs themselves, there are much less trivial social justice problems to worry about. Any SJW who spends a large amount of time dealing with cultural appropriation when they could be dealing with those is just proving that they’ve run out of actual issues to solve and are now focusing on trivialities.

Question: How can I tell my 15-year-old daughter she is awful at writing?

And more importantly, his encouragement combined with his complaints inspired me to keep working on my art. That’s how you do it. Encourage that she’s writing, read everything she lets you read, then give out (objective) criticisms in a compliment sandwich. I have a 19-year-old friend getting a book published. She started writing around your daughter’s age. She didn’t have any family connections to publishers or anything like that; she built a following on Wattpad and used that to find a publisher. Question: How can natural selection design anything?
Answer: Imagine you're outside on a nice summer evening, walking through the woods with a few friends. Suddenly, you hear a buzzing in the distance. You and your friends keep walking and swatting mosquitoes. Suddenly, you feel a pinching sensation on your left calf. You look down and find a mosquito sucking up your blood. You kill it, then curse to yourself since you've already been bitten. But it's only one time, so what's the harm? You and your friends make it back to the great indoors and go to sleep. The next morning you all wake up covered in mosquito bites. “How??” You all wonder. “We killed all of the mosquitoes!” Turns out, the mosquitoes who were quiet, the mosquitoes who were gentle, the mosquitoes whose bites didn't hurt, were the ones that survived. These mosquitoes are the ones who get to reproduce a higher percent of the time than the loud, sloppy, and painful ones. Even if it's only 1% more often, imagine that process stretched out over thousands or even millions of years. That 1% better chance means there’s 1% more of that kind of mosquito the next season, which leads to another 1% more the next, etc etc. After a couple million years, there's only the best mosquitoes left. And then we won't hear any of them coming.
